newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Sime says bank merger in limbo.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Sime says bank merger in limbo.

text.p: Malaysia's largest conglomerate, Sime Darby Bhd, said on Tuesday it was waiting for Oriental Bank Bhd to list on the local bourse before deciding whether to take a stake in it.

"It may well be that the post-listing price established for Oriental Bank will be too big or too high for Sime to be interested in any more," Sime Darby deputy chairman, Tunku Ahmad Yahaya, told reporters after a conference on corporate governance.

Sime Darby announced last year its intention to acquire Oriental, a subsidiary of Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd. Sime said it wanted to merge Oriental with its own banking subsidiary, Sime Bank.

But the deal fell apart after MIDF said in late January it did not intend to sell any of its 78.4 percent stake in Oriental and wanted to list the medium-sized bank on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
Tunku Ahmad said Sime Darby regarded its offer for Oriental as "frozen" by the MIDF move.

"Sime Darby's position is they thought they were following the guidelines of the (Finance) minister and the Governor of the central bank in looking for the opportunity to create a larger, more competitive Malaysian bank," Tunku Ahmad said.
"It's a question whether Oriental will be listed or not. And MIDF must decide what it wants to do," he added.

Malaysia's Finance Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has called for smaller banks to merge with larger ones to better compete with foreign institutions in the coming era of global financial liberalisation.
Asked whether Sime Darby was eyeing another Malaysian bank in the meantime, Tunku Ahmad said: "Sime would be reviewing the situation all the time. I can't comment any further."
